ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, there is a right-angled triangular scrap ABC, where $\angle BAC=90^\circ$. Now, a rectangular strip DEFG is cut from it, where E and F are on BC, G is on AB, and D is on AC. If $BF=4.5\text{cm}$, and $CE=2\text{cm}$, then what is the length of the strip GF in centimeters?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ $\angle BAC=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AGD+\angle ADG=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ rectangle GFED,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BFG=\angle DEC=\angle GFE=\angle DEF=\angle GDE=90^\circ$, DG$\parallel$BC, FG=DE,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADG+\angle CDE=90^\circ$, $\angle AGD=\angle B$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AGD=\angle CDE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B=\angle CDE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BFG\sim \triangle DEC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{FG}{CE}=\frac{BF}{DE}$\\
$\therefore$ FG$^{2}=BF\cdot CE=4.5\times 2=9$\\
Solving for FG yields $\boxed{3}$ (taking the positive value)

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: Given $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, so $\angle AGD+\angle ADG=90^\circ$. Because GFED is a rectangle, $\angle BFG=\angle DEC=\angle GFE=\angle DEF=\angle GDE=90^\circ$, $DG\parallel BC$, and $FG=DE$. Therefore $\angle ADG+\angle CDE=90^\circ$, and $\angle AGD=\angle B$. Hence $\angle AGD=\angle CDE$, so $\angle B=\angle CDE$. Therefore $\triangle BFG\sim \triangle DEC$, giving $\frac{FG}{CE}=\frac{BF}{DE}$. Since $FG=DE$, we get $FG^2=BF\cdot CE=4.5\times 2=9$, so $FG=3$.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, there is a triangle ABC, with A above, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right; BC is the base. The shaded part is rectangle DEFG, with F and E on the base BC, G on side AB, and D on side AC. GF and DE are the two vertical sides of the rectangle, and GD and FE are the upper and lower sides. The problem gives ∠BAC=90°, BF=4.5 cm, CE=2 cm.

Reasoning: Because DEFG is a rectangle, FG ⟂ BC, DE ⟂ BC, and FG=DE. Compare the right triangles on the two sides at the bottom, △BFG and △DEC: △BFG is right-angled at F, and △DEC is right-angled at E. Also because AB ⟂ AC, and FG and DE are both perpendicular to BC, from the perpendicular relationship it can be obtained that acute angle ∠B is equal to ∠CDE. Therefore △BFG ∼ △DEC. From corresponding sides of similar triangles, FG/CE = BF/DE. Also DE=FG, so FG/2 = 4.5/FG, that is, FG²=4.5×2=9. Because the length is positive, GF=3 cm.
